topic: Level flight performances, power available and required for jet and propeller aircrafts.
syllabus_extract: Level flight performances, power available and required for jet and propeller aircrafts. Best climb speeds.
specific_objectives: 6.1.3.1 Trainee will be able to describe flight performance of aircraft.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Activity: Graphical analysis of power curves. Safety: None. Supervision: Instructor guided.
intro_questions: Define thrust and drag equilibrium in steady level flight.
State the relationship between power, thrust, and velocity.
Identify the primary engine types used in modern aviation.

development.content:
Level flight performance fundamentals
Power required curve characteristics
Minimum power speed identification

Jet aircraft power available
Jet aircraft power required
Jet performance envelope limits

Propeller aircraft power available
Propeller aircraft power required
Best climb speed derivation

summary_questions: Compare the shape of power available curves for jets versus propellers.
Explain how to determine maximum level flight speed from power curves.
home_assignment_question: Analyze how excess power influences climb gradient and rate of climb in the next session.

pft_rows.syllabus: Forces in climb, Excess power, max angle, maximum rate, Economical climb, time to climb.
